entries.50.28: "Not far from the river, charioteer, is this very great ingudi tree rich in flowers and shoots. Let us lodge here."
entries.50.29: "Let me behold the best of rivers, auspicious, whose waters are honoured by gods and men and gandharvas, by beasts and serpents and birds."
entries.50.30: Lakshmana and Sumantra said to Raghava, "So be it," and then drove up with the horses to that ingudi tree.
entries.50.31: Rama, the delight of the Ikshvakus, came to that lovely tree and descended from the chariot with his wife and with Lakshmana.
entries.50.32: Sumantra too descended, unyoked the excellent horses, and waited with joined palms upon Rama, who was seated at the foot of the tree.
entries.50.33: There was a king there named Guha, a friend to Rama as his own self, mighty, of the Nishada race, and renowned as a chief.
entries.50.34: Hearing that Rama, the tiger among men, had come to his realm, he came attended by the elders, by his ministers and by his kinsmen.
entries.50.35: Then, seeing the lord of the Nishadas approaching from afar, Rama went with Saumitri to meet Guha.
entries.50.36: Stricken, Guha embraced him and said to Raghava: "As Ayodhya is, so is this yours, Rama. What shall I do for you?"
entries.50.37: "Who indeed shall obtain so beloved a guest, mighty-armed one?" Then, taking up excellent food and provision of many kinds,
entries.50.38: he swiftly presented the guest-offering and spoke these words: "Welcome to you, mighty-armed one. This whole earth is yours."
entries.50.39: "We are your servants and your honour is our lord; rule our kingdom well. Food to chew and to eat, to drink and to lick, is ready, and choice couches for you, and fodder for the horses."
entries.50.40: As he spoke thus, Raghava replied to Guha: "By you we have at all times been honoured and gladdened,
entries.50.41: "by your coming on foot and by this show of affection." And pressing him with his two well-rounded arms, he spoke these words:
entries.50.42: "By good fortune, Guha, I see you in health along with your kinsmen. Is all well too in your realm, among your friends and in your woods?"
entries.50.43: "Whatever little you have made ready out of affection, I acknowledge it all; but I do not engage in the accepting of gifts."
entries.50.44: "Know me for an ascetic ranging the forest, wearing kusha and bark and deerskin, living on fruit and root, and set upon dharma."
entries.50.45: "I have need of fodder for the horses and of nothing else at all; by this much alone shall I be well honoured by you."
entries.50.46: "These horses were dear to my father, king Dasaratha; if they are well tended, I shall be honoured by them."
entries.50.47: Guha there and then commanded his men that drink and fodder for the horses be given swiftly.
entries.50.48: Then, with bark for his upper garment, he performed the evening twilight rite and took water alone for his food, fetched by Lakshmana himself.
entries.50.49: Then Lakshmana washed the feet of Rama and his wife as they lay upon the ground, and withdrawing, stood leaning against a tree.
entries.50.50: Guha too, conversing with the charioteer and with Saumitri, kept vigilant watch over Rama, bow in hand.
entries.50.51: So, as that illustrious, high-minded and great-souled son of Dasaratha lay there, he who had never known sorrow and was accustomed to ease, the night passed very slowly.
